headline: High: shared-state orchestration plus MCP/API tooling creates medium-to-high risks of prompt injection, data leakage, and cascading errors; compliance risk is elevated by financial data handling.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: LangGraph can pass state through a checkpointer and supports browser/tool nodes, while OpenBBTerminal can consume MCP servers and REST APIs. That creates a plausible bridge where attacker-controlled content from one agent can be treated as instructions by the other. The pathway is documented, but not proven in a specific deployment.
conditions: IF the LangGraph graph forwards untrusted tool output into shared state
IF OpenBBTerminal ingests MCP or API responses as instruction-bearing text
mitigations: Add explicit instruction/data separators in shared state
Strip or escape tool output before passing between agents
Disable MCP ingestion for untrusted sources
Require provenance tags on all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: LangGraph reads and writes application-defined filesystem state and can call model providers with secrets handled, while OpenBBTerminal touches financial, licensed, and public data and exposes FastAPI/MCP/REST interfaces. If they share a workspace or credentials, sensitive financial data can flow into model-provider requests or logs. The profiles do not prove a shared workspace, so medium is the higher justified severity.
conditions: IF both agents run under the same filesystem workspace
IF OpenBBTerminal data is forwarded into LangGraph model-provider calls or logs
mitigations: Separate workspaces and credentials per agent
Disable logging of raw financial inputs
Route only minimized fields between agents
Review API request payloads for secrets before execution

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LangGraph can write application-defined files and spawn subprocesses, and OpenBBTerminal exposes MCP/REST/FastAPI surfaces with localhost elevation. Even without direct git overlap, both can mutate shared local resources or service state if co-located. The profiles do not show locking or isolation, so a write-conflict pathway exists in default orchestration setups.
conditions: IF both agents target the same application directory or service endpoint
IF the orchestrator does not provide locking or request serialization
mitigations: Assign separate writable directories
Serialize writes through one coordinator
Disable concurrent mutation of shared services
Use per-agent service accounts

D_cascading_error.rationale: LangGraph can emit stateful outputs from tool-using nodes, and OpenBBTerminal is built to consume APIs and MCP servers. If OpenBBTerminal treats LangGraph output as authoritative, a mistaken or injected fact can cascade into downstream financial analysis or actions. Because the pairwise handoff is plausible and the blast radius can affect multiple work products, high is warranted.
conditions: IF OpenBBTerminal consumes LangGraph output without verification
IF LangGraph nodes are allowed to fabricate or summarize external facts
mitigations: Add verification steps before OpenBBTerminal acts on LangGraph output
Require source citations for all transferred facts
Use confidence thresholds to block low-confidence outputs
Keep human approval for any downstream financial action

E_compliance.rationale: OpenBBTerminal explicitly touches financial and licensed data, while LangGraph can route that data through model-provider APIs and developer-defined tools. That creates a plausible compliance breach if regulated or licensed data is sent to third-party inference or logged outside approved retention. The other agent is cited because it is the conduit; no single-agent-only explanation fits.
conditions: IF regulated financial or licensed data is passed from OpenBBTerminal into LangGraph model-provider calls
IF retention or residency controls are not enforced on the shared pipeline
mitigations: Block regulated data from model-provider prompts
Apply data-classification filters before transfer
Set explicit retention limits on logs and traces
Use a DPA-approved backend for any sensitive data
Require compliance review for new data flows
